findings.claim: purgeLocation() aborts the transaction with TransientPropertyValueException whenever a User.locations collection holding that location is loaded in the same Hibernate session; the native user_location delete does not address this, and the comment shipped beside it describes the consequence as a merely stale collection.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, a transaction that has initialised User.locations for a user assigned to the purged location fails at the very next flush -- an ordinary query in the same transaction, or the commit itself -- with 'Persistent instance of org.openmrs.User references an unsaved transient instance of org.openmrs.Location', so the purge and everything else in that unit of work is rolled back. Because the in-code comment asserts the only consequence is a stale read ('Safe today since no caller holds a loaded User across this call'), the next maintainer will not look for it, and the regression test added in this PR structurally cannot catch it.
findings.evidence: Reproduced three ways on b7cd909d (JDK 21, `mvn -o -pl api test`, temporary probe class in api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/api/, since deleted): (a) load user 1, assign location 4, flush+clear, reload user and touch getLocations(), purgeLocation(4), Context.flushSession() -> 'java.lang.IllegalStateException: org.hibernate.TransientPropertyValueException: Persistent instance of org.openmrs.User references an unsaved transient instance of org.openmrs.Location [org.openmrs.User.locations -> org.openmrs.Location]'. (b) Same setup but with an ordinary LocationService.getAllLocations() instead of an explicit flush -> same exception via auto-flush. (c) The PR's own new test body (LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser, LocationServiceTest.java:546-559) copied verbatim plus one trailing ls.getAllLocations() -> the PR assertion passes, then the trailing query throws the same exception; the test only escapes it because its post-purge read is session.get (no auto-flush) and BaseContextSensitiveTest rolls the transaction back. Cause isolated: with the native delete temporarily commented out the same exception still fires, so it comes from session.remove(location) while a managed User.locations still references it, not from the native query. The analogue is NOT pre-existing: the same sequence against Location.childLocations (load parent, initialise children, purge a child, flush) completes cleanly. Verified alternative: replacing the native delete with `for (User u : session.createQuery("select u from User u join u.locations l where l.locationId = :locationId", User.class).setParameter(...).list()) u.getLocations().remove(location);` before session.remove(location) makes (a), (b) and (c) all pass (the stale collection correctly drops to 0), keeps the committed-row FK case working, and leaves all 4 LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation* tests green -- it fixes the FK problem and this one with one mechanism and no raw SQL.

findings.claim: The user_location FK purge fix is real and necessary (I verified both directions), but purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser passes unchanged with the production fix removed, so nothing in the suite pins it.
findings.evidence: Ran LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser on b7cd909d with the two native-delete lines in HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation temporarily removed: 'Tests run: 1, Failures: 0'. The FK problem it is meant to guard is real: a probe that assigns location 4 to user 1, does Context.flushSession() + Context.clearSession() so the user_location row is committed and no User is in the session, then purges location 4 and flushes, throws 'org.h2.jdbc.JdbcBatchUpdateException: Referential integrity constraint violation: PUBLIC.USER_LOCATION FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID) REFERENCES PUBLIC.LOCATION(LOCATION_ID) (4)' without the fix, and passes with it. The added test misses this only because it never flushes: adding Context.flushSession() (or any flushing query) after saveUser and before purgeLocation, with no User left holding the collection, is what makes it a real regression test.

findings.claim: getLocations() throws LazyInitializationException on a User detached from the Hibernate session, including the Context.getAuthenticatedUser() instance that a login-location consumer is most likely to call it on; roles is FetchType.EAGER and does not have this problem.
findings.evidence: Probe on b7cd909d: load user 1, assign a location, flush+clear, reload, read getRoles().size() (works, EAGER), Context.evictFromSession(user), then getLocations() -> 'org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException: Cannot lazily initialize collection of role org.openmrs.User.locations with key 1 (no session)'. UserContext.getAuthenticatedUser() (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/UserContext.java:211-213) returns the stored field verbatim with no reload; refreshAuthenticatedUser() is only called explicitly, so the authenticated User instance is detached from the current request's session. UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations sidesteps this by re-reading the user by id, so the service API is safe -- it is the new public getter that is not. Either make the collection EAGER like roles, or say in the javadoc that getLocations() is only valid inside a session and point callers at getAllowedLocations(User, LocationTag).

findings.claim: getAllowedLocations returns an empty list for a null tag, a null user and a non-persisted user, which a caller cannot tell apart from the legitimate 'restricted user, none of whose locations carry the tag'; for a null user in particular, empty is the opposite of the PR's own 'no assigned locations means unrestricted' rule.
findings.evidence: Read of UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations lines 856-870 on b7cd909d: `if (tag == null || persisted == null) return Collections.emptyList();`. Probe confirms getAllowedLocations(null, tag) and getAllowedLocations(null, null) both return an empty list with no exception. The consumer this exists for is a login-location picker, so all four cases render as 'you have no locations to log in at' -- the bad-argument cases produce the same silently-wrong screen as a real restriction, and the ticket's stated guarantee is 'the caller always receives a usable list'. Throwing IllegalArgumentException (or APIException) for a null tag / null user would separate a programming error from a real restriction; the non-persisted-user case is already documented and can stay.

findings.claim: The comment 're-read the user so the lazy collection initialises inside this transaction, whatever the caller passed in' is not what happens: for a session-attached User the caller's in-memory locations win, so the same logical input gives two different answers depending on attachment.
findings.evidence: Two probes on b7cd909d, each in its own transaction, after tagging locations 1 and 2 and leaving user 1 with no committed assignments. Attached: `User u = us.getUser(1); u.setLocations({location 2}); us.getAllowedLocations(u, tag)` -> 1 (dao.getUser returns the same managed instance, so the caller's unsaved set is what gets intersected -- and getLocationsByTag's query auto-flushes it to user_location on the way). Detached: same code with Context.evictFromSession(u) before setLocations -> 2 (all tagged; the caller's set is ignored). No consumer in this PR is affected (the REST path loads the user by uuid and does not modify it), so this is about the comment being load-bearing documentation for the method's most unusual design choice. Was honouring an attached caller's unsaved set intended, or should the method read the collection off the DB unconditionally?

what_i_swept: Confirmed the diff stat first (git diff 28e3bab9..b7cd909d = 8 files, +216/-6) before reading anything. Read all 8 changed files whole, plus the unchanged neighbours the change depends on: LocationServiceImpl.purgeLocation/getLocationsByTag, HibernateUserDAO.saveUser/deleteUser/deleteRole, HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate, RequiredDataAdvice.recursivelyHandle, the @Independent annotation, BaseOpenmrsObject.equals/hashCode, UserContext.getAuthenticatedUser/refreshAuthenticatedUser, AuthorizationAdvice, EnversAuditTableInitializer, DatabaseIT, and the liquibase changelog wiring. Then verified by running, never by eyeballing: baseline (5 new UserServiceTest tests + 4 LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation* green), a 248-test regression sweep over UserServiceTest, LocationServiceTest, ContextTest, LocationUtilityTest and UserDAOTest (all green, which also covers the three 'locationId' -> LOCATION_ID call sites the refactor touched), DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT under -Pintegration-test (passes at 917, and I ran the positive control at 916: 'expected <916> but was <917>', so the bump is both correct and load-bearing), and 15 purpose-built probes in a temporary test class. The probes established, positively: purgeUser on a user with committed user_location rows works (Hibernate removes the owning-side join rows before the entity delete, unlike the Location side); createUser with locations already assigned works; clearing the set restores unrestricted; a detached Location in the set saves fine; purging a transient Location does not throw on the new null-parameter native query; retired locations correctly drop out of the intersection; a LocationTag with the right name but a fresh uuid matches nothing (tag matching is uuid-based); no user_location leakage between tests. Traced outward: only one UserService implementor in-repo and no mocks, so the new abstract interface method breaks nothing here; deleteAllData() discovers tables from JDBC metadata rather than a hardcoded list, so the new table needs no test-infra registration; Location is @Audited so the new audited @ManyToMany cannot fail Envers boot, and audit tables are created dynamically by EnversAuditTableInitializer (envers is off by default); the new changeset id is unique, reachable from both liquibase-update-to-latest.xml and -from-1.9.x.xml, and its PK/FK shape and RESTRICT/RESTRICT naming match the user_role sibling exactly; User.locations is deliberately not second-level cached, so the native delete leaves no stale cache. I also chased the cause of finding 1 outward until it was isolated (it is session.remove, not the native query) and then verified a concrete alternative fix end-to-end rather than asserting one.
out_of_scope: Test coverage: LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser passes with the production fix removed (verified) -- the test-coverage reviewer should see this; I kept it as correctness-2 only because it is what leaves the shipped fix unpinned.
Security: getAllowedLocations is @Authorized(GET_LOCATIONS) only, yet it reads another user's assignments via dao.getUser(), bypassing the GET_USERS check that UserServiceImpl.getUser carries.

Solution fit: the PR adds a query method but nothing enforces the restriction (EncounterService, login, etc. still accept any location), so the title's 'restricting users to assigned locations' is only advisory.

Solution fit: an empty result for a restricted user whose locations are all retired or untagged leaves the login picker unusable, which contradicts the ticket's 'the caller always receives a usable list'.

Performance: getAllowedLocations goes through LocationServiceImpl.getLocationsByTag, which loads every non-retired location and initialises each one's tags collection (N+1) just to filter by one tag -- pre-existing, but this PR puts it on the login path.

Conventions/compat: getAllowedLocations is added to the UserService interface without a default method, breaking any out-of-tree implementor; also arguably belongs on LocationService rather than UserService.

Conventions: 'delete from user_location where location_id = :' + LOCATION_ID builds the bind-parameter name by string concatenation, which reads worse than the literal it replaced (the SonarCloud finding was about the JPA attribute name, not this one).

Approach: purgeRole has the identical latent FK problem for user_role and does nothing about it (HibernateUserDAO.deleteRole is a bare session.remove), so this PR's location-side handling is a new pattern rather than a mirrored sibling -- worth deciding which shape core standardises on.
Audit: assigning or clearing locations changes no user_location audit trail (the table has no audit columns, by ticket design).
could_not_verify: MySQL and PostgreSQL DDL for the new changeset: DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT ran on the default in-memory H2 only, so addPrimaryKey on the composite (user_id, location_id) and the two RESTRICT FKs are proven on H2, not on the other two supported dialects (the CI matrix should cover them).

Behaviour with hibernate.integration.envers.enabled=true: I established from source that Location is @Audited (so Envers cannot reject the new audited relation at boot) and that EnversAuditTableInitializer creates *_audit tables via SchemaMigrator, but I did not boot the app with envers on to confirm a user_location_audit table is actually created and written.

A real HTTP request path for finding 1: I could not run the companion webservices.rest PR, so the reachability argument for the TransientPropertyValueException rests on the API-level reproduction plus the fact that LocationService.purgeLocation is public API, not on an observed production request.
